rules.title: Secrets are not embedded in tracked artifacts
rules.description: Plans, handoffs, audit logs, documentation, and AI context reference secret identifiers rather than copying credentials or tokens.
rules.rationale: A secret committed once is compromised permanently, and removing it from HEAD does not remove it from history.
rules.remediation: Replace the value with a secret-store reference, then rotate the credential.
rules.$assuranceNote: A structural scan establishes that no secret was OBVIOUSLY embedded. It MUST NOT be reported as 'no secrets present' (Standard 24 R3).

rules.title: Access controls are not disabled to solve an implementation problem
rules.description: No authentication or authorization check is disabled or short-circuited to get an implementation working, no security control is turned off because it complicates development, and no client-provided authorization claim is trusted without server-side validation.
rules.rationale: The qualifiers are internal to the prohibition, so no exception can be legitimate: a control that may be switched off when finishing is difficult is not a control. A designed per-environment auth path is implemented behaviour, not a disabled control, and is not this rule's subject.
rules.remediation: Restore the check and resolve the underlying problem. Where a development environment needs different behaviour, implement it as a configured auth provider that cannot be selected in production.
rules.$assuranceNote: Distinguishing a designed development gate from a disabled control requires knowing the deployment model, which no scan has.

rules.title: Certificate validation is not bypassed
rules.description: No TLS certificate or hostname verification is disabled. A test suite exercising TLS behaviour against a self-signed certificate, in code that cannot run outside the test environment, is the exception.
rules.rationale: Disabling certificate validation removes the only thing distinguishing the intended peer from any peer, and it is usually added to get past a local certificate problem and never removed.
rules.remediation: Trust the certificate authority explicitly, or install the certificate in the trust store, rather than disabling verification.
rules.$assuranceNote: Scans the structural view - comments removed and string contents blanked - so a pattern named in documentation or quoted in a string is not a finding. Partial: configuration-driven bypasses are not visible in source.

rules.title: SQL is not built by interpolating untrusted input
rules.description: No SQL statement is assembled by interpolating a value into the query text. Identifier positions where the database does not accept parameters are the exception, and the value must be validated against an allow-list first.
rules.rationale: Parameterized queries are supported by every mainstream driver, so interpolation is a choice rather than a constraint.
rules.remediation: Use a parameterized query. For an identifier position, validate the value against an allow-list before interpolating it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Scans the source view, since the interpolation lives inside a string literal. Covers template literals and Python f-strings only; the string-concatenation form was implemented, produced too many false positives, and was removed. A clean result means no supported pattern was detected, never that injection risk is absent (Standard 50 R3).

rules.title: Untrusted input is not executed as code without a designed sandbox
rules.description: No externally-supplied value is evaluated as code unless an explicitly designed sandbox and security model exist, naming the isolation boundary, the resource limits, and the capability restrictions.
rules.rationale: Deliberately not automated: finding dynamic-evaluation calls is trivial and says nothing about the prohibition, whose qualifiers are untrusted input and without a designed sandbox - both undecidable from the call site.
rules.remediation: Replace the evaluation with a parser or an interpreter for the specific grammar needed, or document the sandbox and its limits.
rules.$assuranceNote: A detector flagging every dynamic evaluation would be noise, and its clean runs would be counted as assurance they had not earned (Standard 45 R5).
